meshoptimizer — vendored source
================================

Upstream:  https://github.com/zeux/meshoptimizer
Version:   v1.2  (MESHOPTIMIZER_VERSION 1020)
Commit:    9d9890c73011d75920af614485296d1e03e95448
License:   MIT — see LICENSE.md

What is vendored
----------------
An unmodified copy of upstream `src/`: `meshoptimizer.h` plus every `*.cpp`
translation unit. Nothing is patched, so refreshing this directory is a plain
re-copy of a newer tag (update the commit + version above, then re-run the
workspace tests).

The full `src/` set is copied rather than the handful of files
`crates/optimize` actually calls, for two reasons: the tree stays a verbatim
upstream snapshot (no per-file dependency list to re-derive on every update),
and a static library only contributes the object files whose symbols are
referenced, so the translation units we never call (mesh/vertex codecs,
clusterizer, meshlet utilities, …) cost a few seconds of build time and
nothing at all in the shipped binary.

How it is built
---------------
`crates/optimize/build.rs` compiles these sources with `cc` in C++ mode into a
static lib, and sets `cfg(has_meshopt)` only when this directory is present —
mirroring how `crates/import/build.rs` gates the vendored ufbx behind
`cfg(has_ufbx)`. Delete this directory and the workspace still builds; the
optimization operations then report `OptError::Unavailable`.

The library needs no configuration macros: `MESHOPTIMIZER_API` defaults to
empty and the whole public surface is `extern "C"` with the platform default
calling convention, which is what `crates/optimize/src/ffi.rs` declares
against. The default allocator uses global `operator new` / `operator delete`,
which is why the build links the C++ runtime (`cc::Build::cpp(true)`).
